sections.name: SearchResult
sections.title: Search result shape
sections.what: Describes one search hit: its web address, title, snippet, the name of the source that found it, an authority score, and an optional published date.
sections.why: Likely reason: every provider returns this same shape so the router can combine them.
sections.watch_out: A provider that returns an empty address produces a result the router later drops.

sections.name: SearchContext
sections.title: Search scope shape
sections.what: Describes the scope a search can be narrowed to, currently the industry of the project being researched.
sections.why: The comment says curated feed lists must respect this scope, or an unrelated feed can answer.
sections.watch_out: If the industry is left empty, feed providers apply no industry filter, so unrelated feeds may answer.

sections.name: SearchProvider
sections.title: Search provider shape
sections.what: Describes what every provider must offer: a name, a way to report whether it is set up, and a search method that takes a query and a result limit.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the router treat every provider the same way.

sections.name: SearchRouterOptions
sections.title: Router options shape
sections.what: Lists the optional settings a caller can pass to a search: which providers to use, result count, per-site cap, source ids, and industry.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the router flexible without forcing every caller to set everything.
sections.watch_out: Only some of these options are read in the shown router code, so setting others may do nothing.

sections.name: ProviderStatus
sections.title: Provider status shape
sections.what: Describes a provider's name and whether it is currently available.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets an admin view show which providers are working.

sections.name: ISearchRouter
sections.title: Router contract
sections.what: Lists what the router must provide: a search method, the names of available providers, and the status of every provider.
sections.why: Likely reason: callers depend only on this contract, so the router's internals can change safely.

summary: Defines the shared shapes for search results, search requests, search providers, and the router, so every provider and caller agrees on the same fields.
purpose: A contract file with no running code. It describes what a search result and a search provider must look like.
why: Likely reason: a separate contract lets each provider and the router be written independently without drifting apart.
how: Read it as a set of templates. A result has a web address, title, snippet, source name, authority score, and optional published date. A provider has a name, an availability check, and a search method. The router accepts options such as result limit, per-site cap, provider allow list, and industry scope.
inputs: None at run time. It is read by the compiler only.
outputs: No output at run time. It shapes the data providers return and the router passes on.
risks: Renaming a field here breaks every provider that uses it. Some declared fields, such as the source id list, do not appear in the shown router code, so their effect is unclear.
debug: If the build fails with a missing or wrong field, compare the provider file with the matching template here. Check that caller option names match the router's options.
